newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-EALES LOSS A MAJOR BLOW FOR AUSSIES-FITZY.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-EALES LOSS A MAJOR BLOW FOR AUSSIES-FITZY.

text.p: DUNEDIN, Aug 13 - John Langford's selection for his "house of pain" test rugby debut on Saturday would have surprised the All Blacks, but they weren't showing such emotions, NZPA reports.
Captain Sean Fitzpatrick preferred to reflect on the loss of rival skipper John Eales, saying his unavailability due to a knee injury was a major blow to the Wallabies.

"He's their captain and he has a lot of influence on their game," Fitzpatrick said after hearing that the Wallaby lineout kingpin was ruled out of Saturday's tri-series and Bledisloe Cup double at Dunedin's Carisbrook, known as rugby's "house of
The second rower has been replaced by ACT Brumbies star Langford, who is yet to experience test rugby.

The All Blacks have won the two 1997 trans-Tasman tests so far to retain the Bledisloe Cup. They also have a firm grip on the tri-series, having won all three of their games so far -- two against South Africa and one against Australia.
However, Australia's diminishing hopes in the three nations competition hinge on Saturday's match, and only a win will keep their hopes alive.

But following injuries to key players Eales, No 8 Daniel Manu and backline players, Pat Howard, Tim Horan and Matthew Burke, there is a good chance that the Australians could suffer badly at Carisbrook.
Hart said he wasn't surprised that regular squad member Garrick Morgan, who played in the MCG test, failed to be an automatic choice as Eales' replacement.
"Maybe it's an assessment of form and fitness. Morgan hasn't had a lot of rugby and I thought that showed up at Melbourne."
"I thought he was struggling and so it doesn't surprise me that he wasn't called up.

"Langford had a very good Super 12, was probably rated by a lot of people as being unlucky not to be in the Australian squad at the start. He's a workhorse and I think he'll be a big value to the pack."
The All Blacks are expected to target Langford and exploit his inexperience, as they have done often to newcomers.

Hart will name his test lineup on Wednesday and though he had hinted at some possible changes after seeing some extremely exhausted players following their 55-35 win over South Africa, he is expected to retain his first choice test lineup for Carisbrook.
"I was pretty pleased (with the players' recovery). I think they trained generally pretty well."
